2. Submission Titles: User-editorialized titles are subject to deletion. State only the facts, not opinions or speculation. Do not use ALL-CAPS. If a submission is removed and rule two is cited, re-title the article and post it again. If you are having trouble, try appending a '?' or message us.

This should not be a rule as written. A rule requiring the title to match the content is one thing (ie "Russian Economy in Trouble" should not be the title of an article about a police shooting). However, subjectively deleting submissions based on User made titles is reddit bullshit.

This rule is correct. The following statement is also correct:

subjectively deleting submissions based on User made titles is ... bullshit

0P's opinion and the rule as written are in agreement.

The rule prohibits user-editorialized titles. As written, it does not prohibit editorialized titles that the news source wrote. As written, it does not prohibit user-created titles that are objective descriptions of the article contents.

It is impossible to objectively enforce a ban on "user editorialized titles" while still permitting users to create their own titles. There will inevitably be disagreement between users and moderators as to whether a user-created title is editorialized or not. As written, I believe this rule provides far more clarity and steps towards resolution, than many other rules on the Internet in general.

3. No Image Posts: Submissions must be articles or videos that depict news.

Another rule in search of a problem. Why can't newsworthy pictures be submitted.

An answer: Without any of context, a narrative, analysis, or an editorial opinion, it's hard to establish the newsworthiness of just a photograph.

If we never knew the story of the tank man, or of the events in China that have been building up to that point, would anybody care about the photo?

Photographs can be a powerful component of news stories, but on their own they don't provide a meaningful unit of "news" to consume. Accompanied by an article, readers have some resources to begin to understand the significance of an image. A Voat link to just an image leaves readers without any context.

4. No Social Media Links: Personal Blog Posts, Wiki Entries, Facebook, Twitter, etc. This includes links to Reddit. Please use /v/meanwhileonreddit.

Why not? We are seeing cases where the major outlets report social media.

An answer: Social media is gossip, not news. Articles presenting a narrative on an event or events happening on social media, can be news. Articles about social media events can provide context and analysis that the raw gossip platform does not provide.

The fact that a CNN article that publishes tweets is ok to submit, but a user linking to those same tweets is subject to deletion is absurd.

When major news outlets report on social media, they rarely provide just a link to the social media object in question. There's a title, context, perhaps analysis. A Voat link to a tweet lacks those things.
